notes: Real screenshot of the project's own API documentation page: the drf-spectacular Swagger UI that the 'accounts' service serves at /api/docs/ (config/urls.py; title, version and description come from SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS in services/accounts/config/settings/base.py; the endpoint list is generated from the service's real views under src/apps/accounts/api/v1). The repo is 15 Django services behind NGINX (deployments/nginx/nginx.conf, deployments/docker/compose.yaml); only the accounts service was run, the other 14 expose the same kind of page. Ran a copy of services/accounts on Python 3.15 / Django 6.1.3 / drf-spectacular 0.30 (versions are not pinned in the repo) with the project's own local settings (SQLite) on 127.0.0.1:8134, captured at a 1280x800 viewport (x1.75 -> 2240x1400). Swagger UI assets load from the CDN drf-spectacular points to. Changes confined to the run copy: the shared 'core' package (pureteProject/core, tag v1.3.38) was cloned with the owner's own GitHub CLI login and placed next to the service instead of being pip-installed; its Redis event publisher is stubbed to a no-op (no Redis here); a small WSGI wrapper strips the /accounts prefix exactly as the project's NGINX 'location /accounts/' block does, so the page is reached at the same path as in deployment; cache switched to in-memory. An access token embedded in the repo's requirements files was not used and was scrubbed from the run copy. No data is shown (documentation page only). DOUBT FOR THE OWNER: GitHub lists six contributors on pureteProject/purete and the owner's account is not among them (he is an organisation member); the picture is real output of the repo, but please confirm his role in this back-end before presenting it. Visually it is a stock Swagger UI skin with this service's real title and endpoints.
